evidence.floor_how: No alternative build declared, so the CLI floor remains null. Separate Windows Python 3.12.14 versus Linux container Python 3.12.10 comparison passed; per-observable measurements are in comment/validation-evidence.json. This does not establish all-platform robustness.

warrant: Position, velocity and body angular rate are graded in SI with absolute 5 mm, 1e-4 m/s and 1e-6 rad/s limits; attitude uses 1e-5 rad sign-invariant rotation distance at fixed NASA timestamps, independently of adaptive step bookkeeping. The pinned smooth dynamics use dopri5 with max_step=0.0625 s, and cubic interpolation introduces an observable-specific numerical floor; density, sound speed, viscosity and true airspeed use their own absolute-plus-relative limits and evaluation of the original Planet output on the sampled state. The measured Docker numerical-noise spread is 2.28174e-08; Windows-versus-Linux outputs also pass all per-observable bounds. Published NESC data separately anchor the pristine nominal trajectory; variants are never treated as published nominal cases. Gravity-sign, frame-transform and inertial-term faults cross the physical limits by large margins. The curator approved these scientific equivalence budgets after reading the calibration, rather than setting them equal to tiny two-ULP spreads. The unchanged full 180-second F16 case differs from SIM 05 by 89.81672 m and 0.85571470 m/s; its trim residual is about 0.0065 m/s2. The curator explicitly approved a coarse 100 m / 1 m/s external anchor while preserving 5 mm / 1e-4 m/s candidate equivalence and the trim-residual bounds. The discrepancy is unresolved and is not NASA certification; the 1% F16 force mutant fails candidate position, velocity, attitude and trim gates despite lying inside the coarse external band.
